text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [P1] NexusCorp (vpc-0abc1234) private deployment — NLB nlb-9876 health checks failing (0/3). Traffic shifted to fallback pool; elevated 5xx rate and higher latency for tenant dedicated-pool-dp-9876. @sre-oncall paged. alert-id=A-2026-0009

jamal.sre: On it. I’m taking triage. quick ask — anyone run a netops job against NexusCorp SGs in the last 30m?

maria-netops: i did a scheduled ops-hardening rollout for private-vpc-tagged SGs at 09:23Z (just now). It applied a restrictive egress/ingress baseline. Could be related, starting to look.

ops-hardening-bot: Deployment succeeded: ops-hardening/2026-03-15-0923 applied -> target: sg-0a1b2c3d (tags: env=private owner=netops). ChangeSet: remove-eip-0.0.0.0/0-egress, add-restrictive-deny-egress-default.

alex-platform: FYI NLB health probes for our private pools come from NLB nodes inside customer subnets; some setups expect SGs that reference the NLB SG or the VPC CIDR to allow the probe. If probes are blocked, TG will mark targets unhealthy.

jamal.sre: copying the SG now to diff. running: aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids sg-0a1b2c3d --output json --query 'IpPermissions'

jamal.sre: (output snippet)
```
[]
```

jamal.sre: that's not right — the app SG used to have explicit allow from 10.0.100.0/24 (nlb-subnet) TCP 10256. Looks wiped by the change.

maria-netops: ack. the ops-hardening policy replaced the permissive rule with a tight allowlist, but I used the env=private tag without excluding dedicated customer SGs. My bad.

maria-netops: proposing two mitigation options: 1) add temporary ingress from nlb-subnet 10.0.100.0/24 TCP 10256 -> immediate recovery; 2) roll back the ops-hardening job for this customer (safer but slower if rollback queue). Thoughts?

jamal.sre: 1 is fastest. please add temporary rule and we'll observe TG. If rollback required later we can do that.

maria-netops: applying temporary rule now:
```bash
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0a1b2c3d --protocol tcp --port 10256 --cidr 10.0.100.0/24 --description "temp allow nlb health checks - roll back after 1h"
```

ops-hardening-bot: Change detected: sg-0a1b2c3d ingress rule added by maria-netops (runbook ref: RB-SEC-45).

jamal.sre: watching target group health (tg-zzzz). Initial state 0/3 -> polling...

~45s later...

jamal.sre: tg-zzzz now shows 3/3 healthy. error rate dropping toward baseline. downgrading impact: partial (some 502s during failover).

incident-bot: Update: alert A-2026-0009 severity lowered to P2. Healthchecks restored. Auto-escalation paused.

cs-liaison: Notifying NexusCorp support channel: "We observed transient traffic disruption for dedicated pool dp-9876 due to a security hardening change. We've applied a mitigation and traffic is stable. We'll follow up with RCA and next steps."

maria-netops: leaving the temp rule in for 60m and then will remove after confirmation. Also opening a fix: ops-hardening job needs exclusion rule for dedicated private VPC SGs (ticket SEC-1245).

eng-lead: Good catch. Action items: 1) rollback or patch ops-hardening to exempt tenant-dedicated SGs; 2) postmortem + runbook update; 3) customer notification + SLA impact calc. Keep the timeline in the incident docs.

sre-oncall: Handoff: daytime oncall @morgan.sre we stabilized the immediate issue; leave the temp rule and coordinate with netops for the controlled fix. Link to runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/nlb-healthcheck-probes

morgan.sre: taking it. I'll stay on for the next 2h and validate no regressions. Assigning follow-ups to maria-netops and eng-lead.

jamal.sre: quick notes for the postmortem (blameless):
- Timeline (09:23 rollout -> 09:25 NLB fail -> 09:26 mitigation applied -> 09:27 TG healthy)
- Root cause: ops-hardening job applied too broadly, removed required SG allow for NLB probe CIDR.
- Impact: brief increased 5xxs and latency for NexusCorp dedicated pool. No data exfiltration.
- Immediate fix: added temporary SG ingress rule for NLB subnet.
- Long term: add exclusion list to ops-hardening, add CI guard to detect removing SG rules referenced by active TGs, update runbook with SG diff steps.

cs-liaison: I'll send the customer a short incident summary and next steps. Estimated RCA timeline 48h.

maria-netops: created ticket SEC-1245 and flagged as P1 for the netops team. I'll also disable auto-apply for the ops-hardening job against tag env=private until fix is live.

eng-lead: Also add an automated check in the deploy pipeline: if a security policy change would drop ingress from any known load-balancer subnet or an active TG IP set, fail CI.

morgan.sre: acknowledged. Handoff complete. closing this thread when follow-ups are owned. :thumbsup:

[END OF THREAD]
